**Note to Users**: The primary requirement to run the BWP Analytical Engine (`02_blue-water.Rmd`) is the set of standardized CSV outputs produced by this script.

Because raw field data is often messy and idiosyncratic, this script is provided for **methodological transparency**. It shows exactly how *we* transformed our raw project data into the required final structures. **You do not need to format your raw data to match our starting point.** Instead, use this document as a blueprint: your goal is simply to produce data files that match the **Target Output Dictionaries** defined at the beginning of each section.

### 🗂️ Workflow & Data Summary
This script processes and standardizes six distinct categories of input data required by the hydrological model:
1. **Climatic Forcings**: Daily Precipitation and Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0).
2. **Soil Properties**: Water Holding Capacity (WHC) and Readily Available Water (RAW).
3. **Crop Parameters**: Rooting depths and irrigation constraints.
4. **Crop Coefficients (Kc)**: Dynamic daily vegetative growth curves.
5. **Crop Systems**: Multi-season crop rotation definitions.
6. **Landscape Demographics**: Cultivated area (hectares) broken down by production system and historical period.

### 📂 Directory Setup & Data Placement

This script automatically generates the required folder structure for all processed outputs and figures. However, before running the script, you must ensure your raw data and code dependencies are placed in the correct starting locations:

```text
project_root/
├── data/
│   ├── raw/                 <- Place your original data here (if adapting this script)
│   └── processed/           <- TARGET: Standardized CSV outputs are saved here
│       └── supplementary/   <- TARGET: Intermediary and diagnostic tables
├── figures/
│   └── manuscript/          <- TARGET: Output location for generated plots
├── code/
│   ├── functions/
│   │   └── 02_get_kc.R      <- Required biophysical function dependency
│   └── 01_Format_Input_Data.Rmd (This file)

```

```{r setup-file, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls(all.names = TRUE)); gc()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman"); library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, readxl, here, knitr)

new.dirs <- list(here("data"), here("data/raw"), here("data/processed"), here("data/processed/supplementary"), here("figures"), here("figures/manuscript"), here("figures/presentation"))
lapply(new.dirs, function (x) if (!dir.exists(x)) {dir.create(x, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)})

FILE_CLIMATE      <- here("data/raw/Model in Excel/2 WB_Anantapur_Crop_Level.xlsx")
FILE_KC_RAW       <- here("data/raw/Model in Excel/1 Kc Anantapur.xlsx")
FILE_FARM_AREA    <- here("data/raw/Model in Excel/For rutuja.xlsx")
FILE_FARM_DEMOS   <- here("data/raw/Model in Excel/For rutuja(1).xlsx")

# ==============================================================================
# BIOPHYSICAL CALIBRATION CONSTANTS
# Note: These parameters define biophysical constraints for grazing and 
# automated harvesting regimes, including regrowth rates and baseline 
# bare-soil configurations.
# ==============================================================================
biophysical_parameters <- list(
  grazing_growth_rate   = 0.00458333333333333,
  grazing_drop_kc       = 0.20,
  grazing_max_kc        = 0.75,
  napier_decline_rate_1 = 0.000307692307692308,
  napier_decline_rate_2 = 0.000153846153846154
)

source(here("code/functions/02_get_kc.R"))

theme_baseR <- theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"), strip.background = element_blank())


```

# Climatic Data (Forcing Variables)

The foundation of the water balance model requires continuous, daily forcing variables. Here, we extract daily Precipitation (P) and Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0).

> *📝 **Author's Raw Data (Reference Only)**: Our raw data originated from a sheet named `Climate` containing columns for `Date`, `Rainfall (mm)`, `Moy Temp`, and `ET0`.*

### 🎯 Target Output Dictionary: Climate Time Series (`01_precipitation.csv` & `02_et0.csv`)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **date** | Date | Continuous sequential dates (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| **p** | Numeric | Daily Precipitation in millimeters ($\geq 0$) |
| **et0** | Numeric | Daily Reference Evapotranspiration ($\geq 0$) |

```{r clim}
clim <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "Climate")

# Extract Precipitation
precip <- clim %>% 
  select(date = Date, p = `Rainfall (mm)`) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), p = as.numeric(p))

stopifnot(
  "Error: Precipitation contains missing values (NA)." = !any(is.na(precip$p)),
  "Error: Precipitation cannot be negative." = all(precip$p >= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)

write.csv(precip, file = here("data/processed/01_precipitation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Extract ET0
et0.daily <- clim %>% 
  select(date = Date, et0 = ET0) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), et0 = as.numeric(et0))

stopifnot("Error: ET0 contains missing values (NA)." = !any(is.na(et0.daily$et0)))
write.csv(et0.daily, file = here("data/processed/02_et0.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Create Climatology Summary for visualizations
climate_summary <- clim %>% 
  select(date = Date, p = `Rainfall (mm)`, temp = `Moy Temp`, et0 = ET0) %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date), p = as.numeric(p), temp = as.numeric(temp), et0 = as.numeric(et0), 
    Year = format(date, "%Y"), Month = format(date, "%m")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Year, Month) %>%
  summarise(Temperature = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), Rainfall = sum(p, na.rm = TRUE), ET0 = sum(et0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), .fns = list(avg = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), q05 = ~ quantile(.x, probs = 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), q95 = ~ quantile(.x, probs = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))

write.csv(climate_summary, file = here("data/processed/03_climatology_for_figure.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```


# Soil Parameters

The hydrological model requires specific soil properties to determine infiltration and drainage dynamics.

> *📝 **Author's Raw Data (Reference Only)**: We mapped soil classifications directly from an excel grid containing ID, Type, WHC, and RAW.*

### 🎯 Target Output Dictionary: Soil Properties (`04_soil.parameters.csv`)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **soil** | Integer | Soil identifier code (e.g., 1, 2) |
| **soil.type** | Character | Descriptive classification (e.g., "Red", "Black") |
| **whc.mmpercm** | Numeric | Water Holding Capacity (mm of water per cm of soil) |
| **raw** | Numeric | Readily Available Water threshold |

```{r soil-param}
soil.param <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "crop Kc _ param SOILS", range = "A2:D4")
colnames(soil.param) <- c("soil", "soil.type", "whc.mmpercm", "raw")

stopifnot(
  "Error: Soil WHC must be numeric." = is.numeric(soil.param$whc.mmpercm),
  "Error: Soil RAW must be numeric." = is.numeric(soil.param$raw)
)

write.csv(soil.param, file = here("data/processed/04_soil.parameters.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```

# Crop Parameters & Coefficients (Kc)

## Rooting Depth and Irrigation Constraints

> *📝 **Author's Raw Data (Reference Only)**: Our raw setup used `1` for irrigated and `2` for rainfed flags.*

### 🎯 Target Output Dictionary: Crop Parameters (`05_crop.parameters.csv`)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **crop.ID** | Integer | Unique identifier for the crop |
| **crop** | Character | Standardized crop name in Title Case |
| **irrigation** | Character | Strictly `"irrigated"` or `"rainfed"` |
| **rooting_depth_cm** | Numeric | Maximum effective rooting depth in cm |

```{r crop-param}
crop.param <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "CROP parameters")

crop.param <- crop.param[, !as.logical(sapply(crop.param, function(x) all(is.na(x))))]
crop.param <- crop.param %>% 
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na)) %>% filter(!if_all(2:4, is.na)) %>% select(-Ref)

colnames(crop.param) <- c("crop", "irrigation", "rooting_depth_cm")
crop.param <- crop.param %>%
  mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop, perl = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(irrigation = case_match(as.character(irrigation), "1" ~ "irrigated", "2" ~ "rainfed", .default = NA)) %>%
  mutate(crop.ID = match(crop, unique(crop))) %>%
  select(crop.ID, everything())

stopifnot(
  "Error: Rooting depth must be numeric." = is.numeric(crop.param$rooting_depth_cm),
  "Error: Irrigation strings mismatch." = all(crop.param$irrigation %in% c("irrigated", "rainfed", NA))
)

write.csv(crop.param, file = here("data/processed/05_crop.parameters.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```

## Crop Coefficient (Kc) Generation

Evapotranspiration relies heavily on accurate scaling by the crop's vegetative stage. Our framework generates these daily curves dynamically based on underlying mathematical definitions (FAO segmented logic, polynomials, and linear regrowth rules).

### 🎯 Target Output Dictionary: Master Kc File (`04_crop_kc_by_doy_all_crops.csv`)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **crop** | Character | Standardized crop name matching crop parameters |
| **doy** | Integer | Day of Year (1-366) |
| **kc** | Numeric | The daily Crop Coefficient scalar for that specific DOY |

### Standard FAO-56 Segmented Curves

We first build standard FAO-56 segmented curves for the majority of standard agricultural crops. This implementation relies on explicitly defined day-of-year (DOY) transitions for initial, development, mid, and late season stages.

```{r generate-fao-kc}
# Suppress formatting warnings during raw data ingestion
kc.raw <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
  readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_KC_RAW, sheet = "Crop cycles Kc", range = "A2:AK16")
))

# Clean empty columns and rows
kc.raw <- kc.raw[, !as.logical(sapply(kc.raw, function(x) all(is.na(x))))]
kc.raw <- kc.raw[!kc.raw[[1]] %in% c(NA, "Sowing_date"), ]
kc.raw[[1]][1] <- "Sowing"
kc.raw[[1]][nrow(kc.raw)] <- "Harvest"

colnames(kc.raw)[1] <- "var"; colnames(kc.raw)[2] <- "FORMULE"
kc.raw$FORMULE <- as.numeric(as.character(kc.raw$FORMULE))
kc.raw[-1] <- lapply(kc.raw[-1], function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))

pome_idx <- which(colnames(kc.raw) == "Pomegranate")
names(kc.raw)[pome_idx - 1] <- "Month"
kc.raw.fruit <- kc.raw[, c("Month", "Pomegranate", "Sweet lime")]

colnames(kc.raw) <- gsub("\\.\\.\\.[0-9]+$", "", colnames(kc.raw))

kc.raw <- kc.raw %>% 
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("Month", "Pomegranate", "Sweet lime", "Groundnut_monsoon", "Groundnut_summer")))

write.csv(kc.raw, file = here("data/processed/supplementary/01_crop_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(kc.raw.fruit, file = here("data/processed/supplementary/02_fruit_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

kc.raw.long <- kc.raw %>% pivot_longer(cols = -1, names_to = "crop") %>% mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_|\\.", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))

kc <- kc.raw.long %>% subset(stringr::str_detect(var, stringr::regex("kc", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% rename(Kc = value, kc_var = var) %>%
  mutate(Kc_var = case_when(grepl("ini", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_ini", grepl("mid", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_mid", grepl("end", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_end", TRUE ~ kc_var))

doy <- kc.raw.long %>% subset(var %in% c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest")) %>% rename(doy = value, doy_var = var) %>% mutate(doy = if_else(doy == 365.00, 366.00, doy))

kc.doy.key <- data.frame(doy_var = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"), kc_var = c("Kc_ini", "Kc_ini", "Kc_mid", "Kc_mid", "Kc_end"))

doy <- left_join(doy, kc.doy.key, by = c("doy_var"))
kc.doy <- left_join(doy, kc, by = c("kc_var", "crop")) %>% arrange(crop, doy, Kc) %>% mutate(doy = as.numeric(doy), Kc = as.numeric(Kc))

kc.doy.crops <- kc.doy %>% select(crop, doy_var, doy, Kc) %>%
  mutate(doy_var = factor(doy_var, levels = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"))) %>%
  arrange(crop, doy, doy_var)

kc_wide_build <- kc.doy.crops %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = doy_var, values_from = c(doy, Kc)) %>%
  rename(
    Sow = doy_Sowing, E_ini = `doy_End of ini`, E_dev = `doy_End of Dev`,
    E_mid = `doy_End of Mid`, Harv = doy_Harvest,
    K_ini = Kc_Sowing, K_mid = `Kc_End of Dev`, K_end = Kc_Harvest
  )

kc_segmented_ls <- lapply(1:nrow(kc_wide_build), function(i) build_fao_curve(kc_wide_build[i, ]))
kc_segmented <- bind_rows(kc_segmented_ls) %>%
  mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))


```

### Polynomial Curves

For Groundnuts, a crop characterized by continuous, rapid growth rates, we utilize derived 4th-order polynomial equations to capture their smooth daily progression rather than discrete segments.

```{r generate-poly-kc}
# Groundnut Summer
gs <- data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
  mutate(crop = "Groundnut Summer", d = doy - 10, kc = if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104, 1.25*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.82*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.8*10^(-3)*d^2 - 2.49*10^(-2)*d + 0.3792, 0))

# Groundnut Monsoon
gm <- data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
  mutate(crop = "Groundnut Monsoon", d = doy - 182, kc = if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104, 1.32*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.99*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.96*10^(-3)*d^2 - 3.02*10^(-2)*d + 0.4, 0))

kc_polynomial <- bind_rows(gm, gs) %>% select(-d)


```

### Fruit Tree Curves

Fruit trees demonstrate gradual vegetative shifts evaluated on a monthly basis. This chunk converts those discrete calendar-month states into continuous daily sequences.

```{r, fruit-trees}
# Fruits
raw_params <- read.csv(here("data/processed/supplementary/02_fruit_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
colnames(raw_params) <- stringr::str_to_title(gsub("_|\\.", " ", colnames(raw_params)))
kc_fruits <- bind_rows(generate_fruit_step("Pomegranate", raw_params), generate_fruit_step("Sweet Lime", raw_params)) 


```

### Complex Harvesting & Regrowth Schedules

Pastures and continuously harvested grasses (e.g., Napier) deviate from single-season logic. Their curves are modeled dynamically based on defined daily linear regrowth rates and specific calendar-day harvesting events. The 0.01 threshold strictly enforces the baseline physical reality of dry-season bare soil.

```{r kc-complex}
no_crop <- tibble(doy = 1:366, crop = "No Crop", kc = 0)
grassland_base <- kc_segmented %>% filter(crop == "Grasslands") %>% pull(kc)

growth_rate  <- biophysical_parameters$grazing_growth_rate
napier_dec_1 <- biophysical_parameters$napier_decline_rate_1
napier_dec_2 <- biophysical_parameters$napier_decline_rate_2
graze_drop   <- biophysical_parameters$grazing_drop_kc 
max_bound    <- biophysical_parameters$grazing_max_kc  
grassland_sow <- kc_wide_build$Sow[kc_wide_build$crop == "Grasslands"]

grazed_thrice <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed Thrice", c(182, 243, 304), grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_aug  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Aug", 213, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_sept <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Sept", 244, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_oct  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Oct", 274, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_nov  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Nov", 306, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)

napier       <- generate_napier("Napier", 1, napier_dec_1, napier_dec_2)
napier_short <- generate_napier("Napier Short", 211, napier_dec_1, napier_dec_2)


```

### Final Kc Merge

```{r, kc-merge}

kc.doy.crop.all <- bind_rows(
  kc_segmented, kc_polynomial, kc_fruits, no_crop,
  grazed_thrice, grazed_1_aug, grazed_1_sept, grazed_1_oct, grazed_1_nov, 
  napier, napier_short
) %>% arrange(crop, doy)

write.csv(kc.doy.crop.all, file = here("data/processed/supplementary/04_crop_kc_by_doy_all_crops.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```

# Crop Systems by Rotations

A single field rarely grows just one crop. We must map complex multi-crop rotations and link them to their required soils and crop profiles.

> *📝 **Author's Raw Data (Reference Only)**: We mapped sequences via string splitting (e.g., separating "Groundnut-Tomato" strings).*

### 🎯 Target Output Dictionary: Rotation Systems (`07_crop.systems.csv`)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **crop.system** | Character | The overarching management system name |
| **rotation** | Character | The specific crop rotation sequence |
| **soil** | Integer | Required soil type for the rotation (1 or 2) |
| **crop_1, 2, 3** | Character | Constituent crops within the rotation |

```{r crop-systems}
crop.systems <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "All rotations")
crop.systems <- as.data.frame(t(crop.systems[c(1:4), -c(1, 2)]))
names(crop.systems) <- c("crop1_crop2_crop3", "crop.system", "n.rotation", "soil")

crop.systems <- crop.systems %>%
  mutate(WB = row.names(crop.systems)) %>%
  subset(!is.na(n.rotation)) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(WB, delim = " ", names = c(NA, "rotation"), too_many = "merge", cols_remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(crop.system = str_to_title(crop.system), rotation = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", rotation, perl = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(crop.system.ID = match(crop.system, unique(crop.system)), rotation.ID = match(rotation, unique(rotation))) %>%
  mutate(crop1_crop2_crop3 = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop1_crop2_crop3, perl = TRUE))) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(crop1_crop2_crop3, "-", names = c("crop_1", "crop_2", "crop_3"), cols_remove = FALSE, too_few = "align_start") %>%
  select(crop.system.ID, crop.system, n.rotation, rotation, rotation.ID, soil, crop1_crop2_crop3, WB, everything()) %>% 
  relocate(crop1_crop2_crop3, .after = crop_3) %>% 
  relocate(WB, .after = last_col())

crop.systems.l <- crop.systems %>%
  select(-WB) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("crop_"), names_prefix = "crop_", names_to = "ncrop", values_to = "crop") %>%
  left_join(crop.param, by = "crop") %>%
  relocate(crop.ID, .after = crop) %>%
  mutate(crop.rotation.ID = paste0(crop, ".", rotation.ID))

write.csv(crop.systems.l, file = here("data/processed/06_crop.systems.l.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cs.rot.irri <- crop.systems.l %>%
  mutate(Irrigation = if_else(irrigation == "irrigated", TRUE, FALSE)) %>%
  group_by(crop.system, rotation) %>%
  summarise(Irrigation = any(Irrigation), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Irrigation = if_else(Irrigation == TRUE, "Irrigated", "Rainfed"))

crop.systems <- crop.systems %>% left_join(cs.rot.irri, by = c("crop.system", "rotation")) %>% relocate(Irrigation, .after = crop.system)

write.csv(crop.systems, file = here("data/processed/07_crop.systems.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```

#### Verification: Crop Systems Definitions

```{r preview-crop-systems, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(crop.systems %>% select(crop.system, rotation, Irrigation, soil, crop_1, crop_2, crop_3), 5), caption = "Target Crop Rotations Format")


```

```{r map-kc-curves, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# Internal .Rdata structures are saved here for the downstream engine.
crop.systems.l.kc <- crop.systems.l %>%
  select(rotation.ID, rotation, crop.rotation.ID, crop.system.ID, crop.system, soil, ncrop, crop, crop.ID, irrigation, rooting_depth_cm) %>%
  left_join(kc.doy.crop.all %>% arrange(doy, crop), by = "crop", relationship = "many-to-many")
crop.rotation.kc.ls <- split(crop.systems.l.kc, crop.systems.l.kc$rotation)
save(crop.rotation.kc.ls, file = here("data/processed/08_crop.rotation.kc.ls.Rdata"))
```

# Spatial Land Use & Agricultural Demographics

To evaluate Blue Water Potential (or Net Recharge) at the macro level, we must scale our field-level water budgets up to the watershed scale. This requires two distinct scaling factors: the physical footprint of the crops (Spatial Land Use) and the population distribution of the farmers (Agricultural Demographics).

## Spatial Land Use (Area by Crop System)

> *📝 **Author's Raw Data (Reference Only)**: Our land use data was gathered in a matrix of crop systems against historical time periods.*

### 🎯 Target Output Dictionary: Production Systems Area (`09_crop_system_area_by_production_system.csv`)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **time_period** | Character | Historical grouping (e.g., "1950s", "2022") |
| **production_system** | Character | The farm classification archetype |
| **crop.system** | Character | The implemented crop rotation |
| **area_ha** | Numeric | Total area cultivated in hectares |

```{r ps-composition}
ps_area <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_FARM_AREA, sheet = "Farm Type structure")

ps_area <- ps_area %>%
  subset(!is.na(WB)) %>%
  full_join(crop.systems %>% select(crop.system, WB), by = "WB") %>% relocate(crop.system, .before = 1) %>%
  mutate(crop.system = case_match(WB, "WB Rice/Banana" ~ "Rice/Banana", "WB Grazed_Once" ~ "Grasslands (Grazed Once)", "WB Rice/Napier" ~ "Rice/Napier", .default = crop.system)) %>%
  subset(!is.na(`Cropping system`)) 

ps_by_cs_area <- ps_area %>%
  select(-`Cropping system`, -WB) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -crop.system, names_to = "production_system_period", values_to = "area_ha") %>%
  subset(!is.na(area_ha) & !area_ha == 0) %>%
  mutate(
    time_period = str_extract(production_system_period, "(?<=\\()\\d{4}s?(?=\\))"),
    production_system = str_remove(production_system_period, "\\s*\\(\\d{4}s?\\)$"),
    time_period = if_else(is.na(time_period), "2022", time_period)
  ) %>%
  select(production_system_period, time_period, production_system, crop.system, area_ha) %>%
  arrange(time_period, production_system) %>%
  group_by(production_system_period, time_period, production_system, crop.system) %>%
  summarise(area_ha = sum(area_ha), .groups = "drop")

write.csv(ps_by_cs_area, file = here("data/processed/09_crop_system_area_by_production_system.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```


## Agricultural Demographics (Historical Farm Counts)

We extract the macroscopic farm counts from historical and modern survey sheets. These demographic weights are required to scale the per-hectare water budgets to total volumetric watershed impacts across different socio-economic groups.

### 🎯 Target Output Dictionary: Historical Farm Counts (`10_no_of_farmers_by_production_system_.csv`)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **time_period** | Character | Historical grouping (e.g., "1950s", "2022") |
| **production_system** | Character | The farm classification archetype |
| **number_of_farms** | Numeric | Total count of farms belonging to the archetype |

```{r farm-counts}
# Extract macroscopic farm counts from historical and modern sheets
farms_count_p1 <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_FARM_DEMOS, sheet = "Archetype village 1950") %>% mutate(time_period = "1950s")

farms_count_p2 <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_FARM_DEMOS, sheet = "Archetype village 2022") %>% mutate(time_period = "2022")

farms_count_df <- bind_rows(farms_count_p1, farms_count_p2) %>%
  # Remove NA and TOTAL rows
  filter(!is.na(`Farm type`) & `Farm type` != "TOTAL") %>%
  filter(!str_detect(`Farm type`, "WB")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Fix raw data spelling errors
    `Farm type` = str_replace(`Farm type`, "Pastoralits", "Pastoralists"),
    # Dynamically strip the "(1950s)" or "(2022)" tags from the farm names
    `Farm type` = str_trim(str_remove(`Farm type`, "\\s*\\([0-9]{4}s?\\)"))
  ) %>%
  # Standardize output column names for downstream engine
  rename(
    production_system = `Farm type`,
    number_of_farms = `No farms`
  ) %>%
  select(time_period, production_system, number_of_farms)

write.csv(farms_count_df, file = here("data/processed/10_no_of_farmers_by_production_system.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```

### Classify Production Systems by Hydrological Typology

Farm production systems are highly heterogeneous. Because irrigation drives a disproportionately high water deficit, classifying farms strictly by majority land area underestimates their hydrological impact. Instead, we use a hierarchical threshold to define the **System Typology**. If a production system dedicates a significant threshold of its land (e.g., > 35%) to irrigation, it is classified as "Irrigation-Driven," regardless of its remaining acreage. 

```{r classify-system-typology}
# 1. Map Crop Systems to Core Surface Types
cs_surface <- crop.systems %>%
  dplyr::select(crop.system, Irrigation) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    land_use = dplyr::case_when(
      Irrigation == "Irrigated" ~ "Irrigated",
      stringr::str_detect(crop.system, "(?i)grassland|grazed|pasture") ~ "Pastoral",
      TRUE ~ "Rainfed"
    )
  )

# 2. Calculate area percentages and pivot to wide format
ps_land_use_area_wide <- ps_by_cs_area %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cs_surface, by = "crop.system") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(time_period, production_system, land_use) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(land_use_area = sum(area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    total_area_ha = sum(land_use_area, na.rm = TRUE),
    land_use_pc   = round((land_use_area / total_area_ha) * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-land_use_area) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = land_use, values_from = land_use_pc, values_fill = 0)

# 3. Apply the Hierarchical Typology Logic
ps_typology <- ps_land_use_area_wide %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    system_typology = dplyr::case_when(
      # THRESHOLD RULE: If >= 35% of land is irrigated, the system is Irrigation-Driven.
      # (You can adjust this 35% threshold to perfectly capture your Small-Scale Fruit Growers)
      Irrigated >= 35 ~ "Irrigated",
      # For remaining systems, classify by whichever holds the majority
      Pastoral > Rainfed ~ "Pastoral",
      TRUE ~ "Rainfed"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Reorder columns for clean reading
  dplyr::select(time_period, production_system, total_area_ha, Irrigated, Pastoral, Rainfed, system_typology)

# Save the structured classification for downstream plotting
write.csv(ps_typology, file = here("data/processed/supplementary/05_production_system_typology.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
